title: The forty-five from memory
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Tuesday. The owner asks him to cut a forty-five without the guide. Freehand. He does it wrong twice and right once and she says now do it wrong on purpose. He can't. She says good; that's the difference.

panels.composition: The mat cutter with its guide bar removed, set aside. The OWNER's hand on it. WOOD looking at the bare table.

image.prompt: a mat cutter on a table with its guide bar removed and set aside, a woman's hand resting on the bar, a young man looking at the bare cutter, black and white, no words

panels.composition: A corner, cut freehand: off. Another: off the other way. A third: clean.

image.prompt: close on three mat board corners side by side, two cut crookedly and one clean, black and white, no words

balloons.text: Now do it wrong on purpose.

image.prompt: a woman in reading glasses speaking to a young man at a mat cutter, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The tally on the wall. Wood adding three. Two wrong, one right. He counts them all. The owner would.

image.prompt: close on a hand adding three pencil tally marks to a wall, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'That's the difference.' Two wrong, one right, all counted.
